By the division algorithm, for every $f(x)\in F[x]$ there are unique $h(x),r(x)\in F[x]$ such that
\[
f(x)=q(x)h(x)+r(x),\qquad \deg r<n.
\]
Thus every class in $K$ is represented by a polynomial in
\[
V=\{a_0+a_1x+\cdots+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}:a_i\in F\}.
\]

The representation is unique modulo $(q)$. Indeed, if $r,s\in V$ represent the same class, then $r-s=qg$ for some $g\in F[x]$. If $g\ne0$, then
\[
\deg(r-s)=\deg(qg)\ge n,
\]
while $\deg(r-s)<n$, a contradiction. Hence $g=0$ and $r=s$.

Therefore the quotient classes are in bijection with the $n$-tuples $(a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1})\in F^n$. Since $|F|=p$, this set has cardinality $p^n$. Hence $F[x]/(q(x))$ is a field having exactly $p^n$ elements.\end{proof}
